prompt: Shifts on signed and unsigned values behave differently. Work out each result (32-bit `int`, gcc on x86-64).
explain: Right-shifting a negative signed value copies the sign bit on gcc (arithmetic shift, implementation-defined by the standard), so -8 becomes -4. The same bits as an unsigned number shift in a zero and give 0x7FFFFFFC. For `c`, shifting right by 8 drops the lowest byte, so 0x56 ends up in the low byte and the mask keeps just it.
